Category: N/A (Cannot be Tech Upgraded) • Fabrication: N/A (Cannot be fabricated, must be gifted or stolen from Arasaka)

Humanity Loss: N/A (None) • Install: Mall

CLASSIFIED FILE — SEE ‘[CYBERPUNK 2077’ FOR FURTHER INFORMATION]

Iconic Chipware. Can be used to implant a personality into a dead host, as long as their internal organ structure is still reasonably sufficient to sustain life and the brain isn’t completely destroyed. In theory, this could revive a deceased individual if a 2.0 Relic Biochip exists of their personality, however the implanted personality will only retain memories made prior to the digital copy being generated. The procedure to have a Relic 2.0 Engram made of a personality is impossible to acquire regardless of reputation or wealth unless Arasaka somehow deems you worth it.

If a Relic 2.0 Biochip is inserted into a compatible deceased person’s shard slot, then within 1 hour that body will awaken, as if they are the implanted personality and have just awoken from a long sleep. This new user will have all the same STATs, cyberware, or any other biological afflictions as the user before their death, but are otherwise able to completely change their Skills and Role to equivalent Levels or Ranks in other Skills or Roles. The new user can also change their LUCK stat, either by increasing it by pulling from their INT or COOL stats, or decreasing their LUCK to increase other non-BODY stats.

However, this process is entirely different if a Relic 2.0 Biochip is installed into a living individual. Once inserted, the Biochip cannot be removed from the user’s shard slot by any means without killing them. Upon first installing the Biochip, it provides no benefits. After the next occurrence of the user reaching the Mortally Wounded Wound State and either failing their Death Save or going Unconscious from being stabilized, they do not die, and instead go unconscious for the next 6 hours. After this time, the user re-awakens at 5 HP in the Seriously Wounded Wound State.

After this point, the Relic 2.0 Biochip will begin to project its loaded engram into the user’s vision, just like with the Relic 1.0, however in this instance the other personality’s memories and mannerisms will begin to blend with the primary user’s. They can also communicate with the digital engram as if it was another person only they can see, and can gleam any insight or knowledge this second personality retains.

In this state, the user’s EMP is renamed to Stability (STAB), and is automatically set to STAB 10. For any Empathy-related Skill Checks, the user treats it as if they had the maximum EMP they were originally allotted at Character Creation. Most importantly, while a Relic 2.0 Biochip is slotted, the user no longer suffers Humanity Loss from any source and cannot succumb to cyberpsychosis.

For every Week spent in this state, the user rolls a 2d6. The result of this roll is how much their STAB decreases by. After the user has gone below 5 STAB, this roll is increased to 4d6 per week. Stability cannot be regained, however at GM discretion, if the user spends a prolonged amount of time doing something beneficial for their mind, such as spending time with loved ones, meditating, or other tasks which do not tax the mind, then their Stability Loss for that week can be reduced by 1d6.

◈ STABILITY CHART
IF STABILITY IS LESS THAN… EFFECT
10 The user is allotted two STAT points to raise any STATs of their choice, up to a maximum of 10.
9 For anyone that was aware of the user’s close encounter with the mortal coil, they become aware of the user’s apparent miraculous survival, and thus the user gets a +2 bonus to Reputation when interacting with those individuals.
8 A burning sense of dread begins to build in the user. A strong desire to live by any means necessary starts to form as well. After this stage, the GM can at any relevant narrative time tell the user to roll 1d6 Stability Loss, which costs the user two Actions and has them coughing up blood and stumbling around.
7 The user takes a -2 penalty to Checks to recall their memories, and gains a +2 bonus to Checks to recall the other personality’s memories.
6 The user can raise two Skills relevant to the other personality to Level 4, but must lower one of their other Skills which they have at least 4 Levels in by 4. This cannot reduce a Skill to below Level 0.
5 The user’s maximum HP is reduced by 5. In addition, whenever the user makes a random 1d6 Stability Loss roll and gets a 6, they go unconscious for 1 hour. During this time, the other personality takes over control of the body, with any relevant skill changes determined by the GM applying for such a time. After this hour is up, the body goes Unconscious for 15 seconds (5 Rounds), after which the user wakes up once more, back in control.
4 The user gains a +2 bonus to any Check related to the other personality’s skillset. This can include combat skills, if the other personality is/was more adept than the user at such skills.
3 The user’s maximum HP is reduced by an additional 5. In addition, slight paranoia over death take hold within the user, so they may begin to act more desperately to find some way to survive their affliction. Also, they will occasionally enter small coughing fits and have moments of apparent weakness or distraction.
2 The user takes an additional -4 penalty to any Check to recall their memories, and an additional +4 bonus to Checks for recalling the other personality’s memories. In addition, the user can raise one Skill relevant to the other personality to Level 10, but must lower one of their other Skills they have at least 4 Levels in by 10. This cannot reduce a Skill Level to below 0.
1 The user is filled with a deep sense of dread, as if they have an innate sense that their final death is fast approaching and unavoidable. However, they are also filled with an odd sensation of finality, clarity, and direction. Whatever that character’s truest desire actually is becomes immediately aware to them (preferably chosen by the player), and they feel a strong pull to achieve that goal by any means necessary before they succumb to their afflictions. Depending on their relation to the other personality, this can also result in the other personality agreeing or disagreeing with the user’s goals, and may work for or against them when prompted to do so. Finally, the user is allotted four STAT points to raise any STATs of their choice, up to a maximum of 10.
0 For every hour the user remains alive, their maximum HP is reduced by 5 and their Death Save permanently increases by 1. Go have a blaze of glory.

“He's fucked in the head, the world's fucked in the head — and you're fucked in the head 'cause MY fucked up head is inside it.

Guess if you want to save the world, that's the first step — get fucked in the head.”

— Johnny Silverhand

Fabrication: N/A (Cannot be fabricated, must be gifted or stolen from Arasaka)
Type: Neuralware
Install: Mall
Option Slots: uses 0

Foundry notes:

  • Iconic: it can't be bought or sourced on the street, can't be fabricated without its Blueprint, can't be taken during Character Generation, and once acquired can't be destroyed unless the player agrees to it beforehand.
  • Corgo's Stability Chart lays out what happens at each STAB threshold; the full chart is in the item text above. Stability is not a CPR stat, so nothing here is automated: track STAB by hand, on the EMP line or on a note.
  • Cannot be fabricated or Tech Upgraded, so it has no price; it has to be gifted or stolen.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Becoming Iconic > Iconic Cyberware).
